subject: Tokenization latency spike - eligibility and evidence request
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@wavefront.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: support+billing@wavefront.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden tokenization latency spike impacting /embed route

Hi Irene —

We're seeing a sudden latency regression on our calls to your /embed endpoint starting ~2026-11-09T08:45Z. Median latency is fine but p95/p99 tokenization time jumps, and a subset of requests time out after 10s. This has caused a downstream batch job to fail and delayed our nightly indexing.

Can you confirm whether this qualifies for SLA consideration (we're on the Production plan, committed throughput) and what evidence you need for a credit request? We can pull traces and sample payloads, but we wanted to coordinate with you so we give you what your adjudication team needs.

Summary: 
- Impact window: ~2026-11-09T08:45Z — 2026-11-09T09:30Z (PST)
- Error pattern: elevated tokenization latency causing overall request >10s and some 504s
- Business impact: delayed index refresh for storefront search; estimated revenue exposure ~USD 2.4k for the window

Thanks — please advise next steps.

— Alex
Alex Morgan
SRE, Wavefront Retail
alex@wavefront.ai
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex@wavefront.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tokenization latency spike - eligibility and evidence request

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the initial window. We're opening an internal incident ticket and will validate impact quickly. To speed adjudication on the SLA side, can you provide the following as attachments (if available) in your reply: 

1) A sample of raw request IDs (X-Request-ID) and timestamps for 10–20 affected requests in the window.
2) Client-side timing headers if you have them (e.g., when the request left your app).
3) Any correlation IDs tied to your batch job that failed.

For transparency: we'll pull our server-side traces and tokenization traces; the specific area of interest is our tokenization microservice and any upstream request routing that could cause a queue/backlog.

I'll copy Karthik and Marissa so they can start gathering logs and a preliminary timeline. Once we reconcile traces we can confirm eligibility for an SLA credit and propose a credit calculation or proportional remedy. Expect an initial update within 6 business hours.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: please include request id list (text) and a short timeline (csv)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, Alex Morgan <alex@wavefront.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tokenization latency spike - initial traces attached

Alex / Irene — attaching our initial artifacts. See attached: traces-tokenization-20261109.json (sampled tokenization traces from the serving runtime) and slo-window-20261109.csv (aggregate SLO bucket counts for the window). Highlights from our quick triage: 

- We observed a short-lived burst of GC activity on a subset of tokenization workers starting 2026-11-09T08:46:12Z which coincides with Alex's reported window.
- Tokenizer queue depth spiked for ~38s on three workers servicing us-west-2, causing p99 to jump from ~230ms -> ~3.4s for tokenization-only time.
- No upstream routing fallback was triggered in the timeframe; requests were consistently routed to the same worker pool.

Preliminary conclusion: the pattern looks like a transient worker-level resource pressure (GC/heap compaction) causing queueing. We will continue to pull full trace bundles and confirm whether this meets the contractual definition of outage vs degraded performance.

Next steps:
- I'll request a full trace bundle and correlate X-Request-IDs; Marissa, can you prepare the calculated proportional credit options per the Production plan terms?

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: traces-tokenization-20261109.json; slo-window-20261109.csv
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex@wavefront.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tokenization latency spike - next steps and postmortem timeline

Alex — thank you for the quick turnaround and for attaching your request IDs (we matched ~15 IDs to our traces). Based on the reconciled traces and the contractual SLO definitions, this appears to be a degradation event (tokenization queuing causing elevated tail latency) rather than a full region outage.

Per our SLA: if an SLO breach is confirmed for the billing period we offer a proportional credit. Marissa is preparing the exact credit amount; preliminarily we estimate a proportional remedy equivalent to ~0.7 days of service credit for the affected usage type (final number pending audit).

Action items / timeline: 
- Marissa will send the formal credit calculation and the draft credit statement for Wavefront by EOD 2026-11-10.
- Karthik and infra will complete a deeper RCA and postmortem; we plan to publish a customer-facing postmortem by 2026-11-17.
- If you require documentation for procurement/finance, we can also provide a signed credit letter.

Would you like us to initiate a formal SLA claim on your behalf, or will Wavefront submit through support+billing (either is fine)? If you'd like us to file it, please confirm and include the preferred HubSpot/Procurement contact.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with the formal credit and the postmortem.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
